sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我要测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com 斜杠 subscribe。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 哎呀。

sentences.en: Clementine, stop.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀，停下。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, sorry.
sentences.zh: 天哪，抱歉。

sentences.en: She has thoughts.
sentences.zh: 她有自己的想法。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Taurese.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·托雷斯。

sentences.en: And this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Over the past decade, the cost of veterinary care in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，美国的兽医护理费用

sentences.en: has skyrocketed as healthcare for pets has come to look more like healthcare for people.
sentences.zh: 随着宠物医疗越来越像人类医疗，费用也随之飙升。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Katie Thomas on how vet care became a multi-billion dollar industry and the fraught emotional and financial landscape it has created for pet owners.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯蒂·托马斯将讲述兽医护理是如何成为一个价值数十亿美元的产业，以及它给宠物主人带来的情感和经济上的困境。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月12日，星期五。

sentences.en: Katie, welcome to our Friday episode.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，欢迎来到我们的周五节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm excited.
sentences.zh: 好的，我很兴奋。

sentences.en: So Katie, you recently wrote about something that I, as a pet owner, and a lot of people on this team, also pet owners, can relate to.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你最近写了一篇关于某件事的文章，作为宠物主人的我，以及我们团队里的许多人（也是宠物主人），都能感同身受。

sentences.en: And that is that the cost of veterinary care has skyrocketed.
sentences.zh: 那就是兽医护理的费用已经飙升了。

sentences.en: Tell me how you came to this story.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你是怎么接触到这个故事的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so a couple of years ago, my family and I, we got a new dog.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几年前，我和家人养了一只新狗。

sentences.en: We got a puppy, and his name is Roscoe.
sentences.zh: 我们养了一只小狗，名字叫罗斯科。

sentences.en: And he did great.
sentences.zh: 它表现得很好。

sentences.en: You know, the first year, he was a very healthy little dog.
sentences.zh: 你知道，第一年它是一只非常健康的小狗。

sentences.en: And then when he was about a year and a half old, he got very sick.
sentences.zh: 后来在它一岁半左右的时候，它病得很重。

sentences.en: And we learned that he had been born with a very serious liver defect.
sentences.zh: 我们得知它天生就有严重的肝脏缺陷。

sentences.en: And our vet referred us to a bigger animal hospital.
sentences.zh: 我们的兽医把我们转诊到了一家更大的动物医院。

sentences.en: And that's kind of when I entered this world, that's like a new level of veterinary care that I hadn't realized existed.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，我进入了这个领域，那是我从未意识到存在的新层级的兽医护理。

sentences.en: So as I was navigating this, I was wearing two hats.
sentences.zh: 所以在处理这件事时，我身兼两职。

sentences.en: You know, one was just as a pet owner and trying to figure out the right treatment for my dog.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我只是一个试图为我的狗寻找正确治疗方法的宠物主人。

sentences.en: And then the other hat I was wearing is as the health care reporter, which is my full-time job.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我的本职工作是医疗记者。

sentences.en: So I kept on noticing a lot of aspects of the veterinary world that to me were starting to feel very, very similar to the human health care world that I cover.
sentences.zh: 我不断注意到兽医界的许多方面，对我来说，它们开始变得和我所报道的人类医疗界非常、非常相似。

sentences.en: And as I started looking into this, I started learning just how much money there is now in the veterinary industry.
sentences.zh: 当我开始深入研究时，我了解到兽医行业现在有多少资金注入。

sentences.en: And also how expensive this care has become over the last couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 以及在过去几十年里，这种护理变得多么昂贵。

sentences.en: I learned that very quickly, these bills can start adding up to $5,000, $10,000, even $15,000.
sentences.zh: 我很快了解到，这些账单很快就会累积到5,000美元、10,000美元，甚至15,000美元。

sentences.en: And how much have prices actually increased?
sentences.zh: 价格实际上上涨了多少？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems to me like a huge amount, but what are the numbers there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我看来涨幅巨大，但具体数字是多少？

sentences.en: So as we know, prices for all kinds of things are going up because we've seen inflation over the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，由于过去几年我们经历了通货膨胀，各种商品的价格都在上涨。

sentences.en: But vet care prices have risen much faster than the overall rate of inflation.
sentences.zh: 但兽医护理价格的上涨速度远快于整体通胀率。

sentences.en: My colleagues and I actually ran the numbers.
sentences.zh: 我和同事们确实核算了这些数字。

sentences.en: And in the last decade, the price of services has risen about 30%.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，服务价格上涨了约30%。

sentences.en: And in that same period, veterinary care has gone up by more than 60%.
sentences.zh: 而在同一时期，兽医护理费用上涨了超过60%。

sentences.en: Why is that, Katie?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，凯蒂？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the question here, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是问题所在，对吧？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So when I started reporting this out, I found that there were a number of factors that were contributing.
sentences.zh: 当我开始报道这件事时，我发现有许多因素在起作用。

sentences.en: And they're all intertwined.
sentences.zh: 而且它们都是相互交织的。

sentences.en: And one is just that the culture of owning a pet has changed.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是养宠物的文化已经改变了。

sentences.en: More and more people are owning pets.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人开始养宠物。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's different surveys, but anywhere between like 60 to 70% of American households have a pet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，虽然调查结果各不相同，但大约60%到70%的美国家庭拥有宠物。

sentences.en: And as those of us who do have pets know, we kind of see them more and more as members of the family.
sentences.zh: 正如我们这些养宠物的人所知，我们越来越把它们视为家庭成员。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, one example is like dogs used to live outside, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，一个例子是狗过去常住在外面，对吧？

sentences.en: Or sleep in a garage or something.
sentences.zh: 或者睡在车库之类的。

sentences.en: And now there's this one survey that I found that almost half of Americans sleep with their pets.
sentences.zh: 而现在我发现的一项调查显示，近一半的美国人与他们的宠物同睡。

sentences.en: I would never do that, Katie.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会那样做，凯蒂。

sentences.en: No, none of us would.
sentences.zh: 不，我们都不会。

sentences.en: And we just need to walk into any pet store to see, you know, how much money people are spending on pets for cute outfits, birthday cookies.
sentences.zh: 我们只要走进任何一家宠物店，就能看到人们在宠物身上花了多少钱，买可爱的衣服、生日饼干。

sentences.en: When you go away, you don't just leave them in a kennel, but they're now dog hotels.
sentences.zh: 当你外出时，你不再只是把它们留在狗舍，现在有宠物酒店了。

sentences.en: You know, there's this fancy one near me where, like, they have a view of the Chicago River.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我附近有一家很高级的，它们甚至能看到芝加哥河的景色。

sentences.en: You know, you can pay extra for a river view.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以多付钱选择河景房。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I would never leave my dog in a dog hotel, though I did just send her to a boarding place where she got a bunch of training when I was on vacation.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会把我的狗留在宠物酒店，尽管我确实刚把它送到一个寄宿处，我在度假时它在那里接受了一些训练。

sentences.en: So I am feeling a little sheepish here.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在感觉有点不好意思。

sentences.en: But it has gone crazy.
sentences.zh: 但这确实变得疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, we were talking to the team earlier, and I was saying I was overhearing someone on the street just walking, talking to their friend,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前和团队聊天时，我说我无意中听到街上有人在走路，和朋友交谈，

sentences.en: having a conversation about dropping her off at daycare.
sentences.zh: 谈论着把她送到日托中心的事。

sentences.en: And I couldn't tell whether she was talking about a dog or a child.
sentences.zh: 我根本听不出她是在谈论狗还是孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So we are all pet owners now, or at least a majority of us are.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在都是宠物主人了，或者至少我们中的大多数人是。

sentences.en: So that bigger demand for services presumably causes prices to rise.
sentences.zh: 那么对服务的更大需求大概会导致价格上涨。

sentences.en: Is that what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这就是这里发生的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a part of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是原因之一。

sentences.en: But the big driver is also that there's just been these remarkable advances in medicine for animals.
sentences.zh: 但主要驱动因素还在于动物医学取得了显著进步。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like what I saw with my own puppy.
sentences.zh: 这和我自己在小狗身上看到的有点像。

sentences.en: Historically, vets would help with really kind of basic things like a cut on a paw or deworming or spaying and neutering.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，兽医会帮助处理一些非常基础的事情，比如爪子上的伤口、驱虫或绝育手术。

sentences.en: But for anything life-threatening like cancer or something like that,
sentences.zh: 但对于任何危及生命的情况，比如癌症之类的，

sentences.en: really the only option that they had available to them was to put the animals to sleep and to give them a humane death.
sentences.zh: 他们唯一能提供的选择就是对动物实施安乐死，让它们人道地离去。

sentences.en: But over the last decade, there's just been huge leaps in what we can do for our pets.
sentences.zh: 但在过去十年里，我们在宠物护理方面取得了巨大的飞跃。

sentences.en: There's been big steps in cancer care, very intricate and involved surgery.
sentences.zh: 癌症护理方面有了重大进展，还有非常复杂和精细的手术。

sentences.en: Dermatology, there's been some really big new drugs for dogs in particular to help with skin allergies.
sentences.zh: 皮肤科方面，特别是针对狗的皮肤过敏，出现了一些非常棒的新药。

sentences.en: You know, there's physical therapy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有物理治疗。

sentences.en: There's just so many options now available to pet owners to help their animals live longer and better lives.
sentences.zh: 现在宠物主人有太多的选择可以帮助他们的动物活得更长、更好。

sentences.en: Like, for example, I spoke to this one vet who she's been working since the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 比如，我采访过一位从90年代就开始工作的兽医。

sentences.en: And she told me this story about how her father was a human doctor.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我一个故事，说她父亲是一名人类医生。

sentences.en: And back then, what she would do is she had a lot of dachshunds, and dachshunds often have bad backs.
sentences.zh: 那时，她养了很多腊肠犬，腊肠犬经常背部不好。

sentences.en: And she would sneak them into the human hospital after hours and into the MRI machine so she could check them out.
sentences.zh: 她会趁下班后偷偷把它们带进人类医院，放进核磁共振仪里，这样她就能给它们检查。

sentences.en: And today, she has an MRI machine.
sentences.zh: 而今天，她自己就有一台核磁共振仪。

sentences.en: And, you know, many animal hospitals have MRI machines for animals.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，许多动物医院都有动物专用的核磁共振仪。

sentences.en: So that's really a measure of how things have changed, even since the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实衡量了自90年代以来情况发生了多大的变化。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's pretty amazing and great that we have these options available for our pets.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们能为宠物提供这些选择真是太棒了，也令人惊叹。

sentences.en: But it also costs a lot of money to do all of this new stuff.
sentences.zh: 但做所有这些新项目也需要花费大量的金钱。

sentences.en: Which brings me to another big change that I found in my reporting, which is this has become very appealing to big businesses.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了我在报道中发现的另一个重大变化，那就是这已经变得对大企业非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: Because just remember, historically, veterinary offices were small businesses.
sentences.zh: 因为请记住，从历史上看，兽医诊所都是小企业。

sentences.en: And they were staffed by animal lovers, not business people.
sentences.zh: 而且员工都是动物爱好者，而不是商人。

sentences.en: And that has made it an enticing target for investors because they see an opportunity there.
sentences.zh: 这使得它成为投资者的诱人目标，因为他们看到了其中的机会。

sentences.en: Okay, so big business spots an opportunity here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以大企业在这里发现了机会。

sentences.en: So what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: So basically, big companies and private equity firms start buying up small chains and individual clinics.
sentences.zh: 基本上，大公司和私募股权公司开始收购小型连锁店和个体诊所。

sentences.en: They pretty much go on an acquisition spree.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎是在进行收购狂潮。

sentences.en: One big example is the conglomerate Mars, which is probably best known for selling candy and also pet food.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的例子是玛氏集团，它可能以销售糖果和宠物食品而闻名。

sentences.en: Little known fact, Mars is also a big dog food manufacturer, not just a candy bar maker.
sentences.zh: 鲜为人知的是，玛氏也是一家大型狗粮制造商，不仅仅是巧克力棒制造商。

sentences.en: Yes, it makes a lot of different dog foods.
sentences.zh: 是的，它生产很多种不同的狗粮。

sentences.en: And it's been in the pet world for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且它在宠物领域已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: But over the last several years, they've also bought up the big veterinary chain VCA.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，他们还收购了大型兽医连锁店VCA。

sentences.en: They also own Banfield, which is in a lot of the PetSmart's, which is a big pet store chain.
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有Banfield，它位于许多PetSmart店里，那是一家大型宠物连锁店。

sentences.en: They also own a specialty hospital chain called Blue Pearl.
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有一家名为Blue Pearl的专科医院连锁店。

sentences.en: And then in addition to that, a lot of private equity backed firms have been buying small individual practices.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，许多私募股权支持的公司一直在收购小型个体诊所。

sentences.en: That trend really peaked in 2021, for example.
sentences.zh: 这一趋势在2021年达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: And so the situation that we have today is that a quarter of all primary care vet clinics are now owned by corporations and three quarters of specialty hospitals are owned by companies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天面临的情况是，四分之一的初级保健兽医诊所现在由企业拥有，四分之三的专科医院由公司拥有。

sentences.en: And Katie, how does this consolidation, you know, in some cases, three quarters of all clinics owned by big companies,
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，这种整合，你知道，在某些情况下，四分之三的诊所由大公司拥有，

sentences.en: how does that affect these high prices we've been talking about?
sentences.zh: 这如何影响我们一直在谈论的高价格？

sentences.en: Well, I spoke to a number of vets who have worked in these corporate owned clinics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我采访了一些在这些企业拥有的诊所工作过的兽医。

sentences.en: And what they told me is that they are under increasing pressure to do things that basically drive up the cost of care for pet owners.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我的是，他们承受着越来越大的压力，被迫做一些基本上会推高宠物主人护理成本的事情。

sentences.en: Some examples that they gave me is they felt increasingly stressed and pressured to see more animals per day.
sentences.zh: 他们给我举的一些例子是，他们感到越来越大的压力，被迫每天看更多的动物。

sentences.en: Others told me, you know, to a certain extent, veterinarians have always had some of their pay tied to how much revenue they bring into the practice.
sentences.zh: 其他人告诉我，你知道，在某种程度上，兽医的薪水一直与他们为诊所带来的收入挂钩。

sentences.en: But at these corporate owned clinics, the pressure is even greater.
sentences.zh: 但在这些企业拥有的诊所里，这种压力更大。

sentences.en: They were being asked to order more tests or one veterinarian that I spoke to said, you know, that she was told she needs to get her cost per client higher.
sentences.zh: 他们被要求安排更多的检查，或者我采访的一位兽医说，有人告诉她需要提高每个客户的平均消费额。

sentences.en: Or someone else said that someone needed training on getting a pet owner to yes.
sentences.zh: 或者有人说，需要培训如何让宠物主人点头同意。

sentences.en: You know, these are high pressure sales tactics that, you know, you really don't expect to see in a vet office.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些是高压销售策略，你真的不会期望在兽医诊所看到这些。

sentences.en: And some of these vets that I spoke to said that they felt pretty uncomfortable with that as well.
sentences.zh: 我采访的一些兽医也表示，他们对此感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: So now there's this doubt, right?
sentences.zh: 所以现在有了这种怀疑，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, is my vet recommending this thing because my dog should have this thing?
sentences.zh: 就像，我的兽医推荐这个是因为我的狗真的需要吗？

sentences.en: Or is my vet recommending this thing because he needs to make a different bottom line than he used to?
sentences.zh: 还是我的兽医推荐这个是因为他需要达到与过去不同的财务指标？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, when I spoke to vets, they were very clear that they only provide the care that they think is best for that particular animal.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我采访兽医时，他们非常明确地表示，他们只提供他们认为对该特定动物最好的护理。

sentences.en: But there's no denying that these incentives and pressures are there.
sentences.zh: 但不可否认，这些激励措施和压力确实存在。

sentences.en: And they said that there's a lot of factors that pet owners don't always appreciate.
sentences.zh: 他们说，有很多因素是宠物主人并不总是能理解的。

sentences.en: One of them is they are very forward, public facing, kind of almost like a retail store.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他们非常前卫，面向公众，几乎就像一家零售店。

sentences.en: They get Google reviews, Yelp reviews.
sentences.zh: 他们会收到谷歌评论、Yelp评论。

sentences.en: And so they're very worried about not providing the top level care and perhaps getting eviscerated in reviews.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常担心不能提供最高水平的护理，并可能在评论中被骂得体无完肤。

sentences.en: And so sometimes that can put pressure on them to make sure that they've done absolutely everything they can for an animal.
sentences.zh: 所以有时这会给他们带来压力，确保他们为动物做了所有能做的一切。

sentences.en: The last thing is that a lot of veterinarians do still own their own clinics.
sentences.zh: 最后一点是，许多兽医仍然拥有自己的诊所。

sentences.en: And they told me that they're facing all of the same rising costs and pressures that any other small business owner is facing.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们面临着与其他小企业主一样的成本上升和压力。

sentences.en: And that includes paying a living wage for workers in a pretty tight labor market, the rising costs of prescription drugs and lab tests and other equipment.
sentences.zh: 这包括在劳动力市场相当紧张的情况下为员工支付生活工资，以及处方药、实验室检查和其他设备成本的上涨。

sentences.en: And they say that a lot of times pet owners just see the high price tag and they blame the person in front of them, which is the veterinarian.
sentences.zh: 他们说，很多时候宠物主人只是看到了高昂的价格标签，然后责怪面前的人，也就是兽医。

sentences.en: Okay, so the rise of this corporate consolidation we've been seeing has meant perhaps higher prices and has put more pressure on vets.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我们所看到的这种企业整合的兴起，意味着价格可能更高，也给兽医带来了更大的压力。

sentences.en: But are there any upsides in it for us, for consumers?
sentences.zh: 但这对我们消费者来说有什么好处吗？

sentences.en: I mean, just one example from my old neighborhood in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就拿我在华盛顿特区旧社区的一个例子来说。

sentences.en: There was a new chain that moved in that was 24 hours, and that was a great option for my very accident-prone dog.
sentences.zh: 有一家新的连锁店搬了进来，是24小时营业的，对于我那只非常容易发生意外的狗来说，那是一个很好的选择。

sentences.en: She suddenly had a couple of different options of places that we could go in the middle of the night if something happened.
sentences.zh: 她突然有了几个不同的选择，如果半夜发生什么事，我们可以去这些地方。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: I mean, anytime there's more money available, you can invest in better services, nicer offices, nicer waiting rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，只要有更多的资金，你就能投资更好的服务、更舒适的办公室和更温馨的候诊室。

sentences.en: There's more money for better equipment and investing in some of these specialty services that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 这样就有更多的钱用于购买更好的设备，并投资于我们刚才提到的那些专业服务。

sentences.en: So there are definitely benefits to this.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是有好处的。

sentences.en: But as I found in my reporting, even as vet care has really caught up in a lot of ways to human health care, there's a lot of important ways that they're different.
sentences.zh: 但正如我在报道中发现的那样，尽管兽医护理在很多方面确实已经赶上了人类医疗保健的水平，但它们在许多重要方面仍然存在差异。

sentences.en: And that can present some really difficult choices and some prickly moral choices for pet owners.
sentences.zh: 这可能会给宠物主人带来一些非常艰难的选择和棘手的道德抉择。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是 Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So Katie, let's dig into the ways that pet care is actually different from human care.
sentences.zh: 那么 Katie，让我们深入探讨一下宠物护理与人类护理的实际区别。

sentences.en: You know, setting aside the fact that pets are not people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，撇开宠物不是人这一事实不谈。

sentences.en: So talk to me about what these main differences are.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这些主要区别是什么。

sentences.en: The biggest difference is how the pet care gets paid for.
sentences.zh: 最大的区别在于宠物护理的付费方式。

sentences.en: I'm not sure anyone in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我不确定在美国有谁

sentences.en: would say that health care is particularly affordable.
sentences.zh: 会说医疗保健是特别负担得起的。

sentences.en: But the fact of the matter is that most people do have health insurance that covers the bulk of their medical costs.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，大多数人都有医疗保险，可以覆盖大部分医疗费用。

sentences.en: And if you are in an emergency situation, hospitals are legally obligated to give you life-saving care and then sort out the bills later.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你处于紧急情况，医院在法律上有义务为你提供救命护理，然后再处理账单问题。

sentences.en: But that's just not how things work in the vet world.
sentences.zh: 但在兽医领域，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Veterinarians don't have the same obligation to treat.
sentences.zh: 兽医没有同样的治疗义务。

sentences.en: And so it's almost entirely on the pet owner to pay the full amount of the bill basically up front and at the time of service, out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 因此，宠物主人几乎必须完全自掏腰包，在接受服务时预付全部账单。

sentences.en: So that is a big difference.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很大的区别。

sentences.en: But isn't there pet insurance as well?
sentences.zh: 但是难道没有宠物保险吗？

sentences.en: There is pet insurance, but a very small minority of pet owners actually have pet insurance, just about 4%.
sentences.zh: 确实有宠物保险，但实际上只有极少数宠物主人购买了宠物保险，大约只有 4%。

sentences.en: And it's very different from the health insurance that most of us are familiar with.
sentences.zh: 而且它与我们大多数人熟悉的医疗保险非常不同。

sentences.en: You know, some examples are that with very few exceptions, you still have to front the money for the bill.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些例子是，除了极少数例外，你仍然必须先垫付账单金额。

sentences.en: And then you would submit that claim to your pet insurance, which will then decide whether, you know, that's a legitimate claim.
sentences.zh: 然后你再向你的宠物保险公司提交索赔，他们会决定这是否是一项合理的索赔。

sentences.en: And then they will reimburse you.
sentences.zh: 然后他们才会报销给你。

sentences.en: Generally, plans don't cover pre-existing conditions.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，保险计划不承保既往症。

sentences.en: They charge more for pets that are older.
sentences.zh: 而且对于年龄较大的宠物，他们收取的保费更高。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the pre-Obamacare version of human health care.
sentences.zh: 这有点像奥巴马医改之前的人类医疗保健版本。

sentences.en: Many things that are now not allowed in the human health care world are still very much a feature of how pet insurance works.
sentences.zh: 许多在人类医疗保健领域现在不被允许的事情，在宠物保险的运作方式中仍然是非常普遍的特征。

sentences.en: And even if you have pet insurance, that doesn't always mean that you can keep it.
sentences.zh: 而且即使你有宠物保险，也不意味着你能一直拥有它。

sentences.en: To take one example, Nationwide, which is one of the biggest providers of pet insurance in this country,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，Nationwide 是美国最大的宠物保险提供商之一，

sentences.en: recently said that the cost of pet care is getting so expensive that it had to discontinue the plans of 100,000 pet owners.
sentences.zh: 最近表示宠物护理成本变得太贵了，以至于不得不取消了 10 万名宠物主人的保险计划。

sentences.en: And so that left a lot of these pet owners basically back where they had started with having to cover the cost of the care themselves.
sentences.zh: 这让许多宠物主人基本上回到了原点，不得不自己承担护理费用。

sentences.en: And that's, of course, presuming they can pay, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，这是假设他们付得起，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure for a lot of people, their devotion to their animal notwithstanding, it's just not possible to drop a few thousand dollars on these amazing life-saving treatments.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我相信对很多人来说，尽管他们对动物充满深情，但要拿出几千美元来支付这些神奇的救命治疗费用，简直是不可能的。

sentences.en: So are those people who can't afford that just having to put their pets down?
sentences.zh: 那么那些负担不起的人只能给他们的宠物安乐死吗？

sentences.en: And what are those people doing?
sentences.zh: 这些人都在做什么呢？

sentences.en: And this is where this just gets extremely thorny and difficult.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题变得极其棘手和困难的地方。

sentences.en: I think there's a number of different answers.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几种不同的答案。

sentences.en: Yes, I think some people do have to put their animals to sleep or choose less expensive options.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为有些人确实不得不让他们的动物安乐死，或者选择花费较少的方案。

sentences.en: But when I talked to pet owners about this, many of them went to pretty extreme lengths in order to cover this care and to find a way to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 但当我与宠物主人谈论这个问题时，许多人为了支付这些护理费用并找到支付方式，采取了相当极端的手段。

sentences.en: You know, I spoke to people who dipped into their retirement funds.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我采访过动用退休基金的人。

sentences.en: I spoke to somebody who donated blood plasma, someone else who took on a second job in order to pay for this.
sentences.zh: 我采访过一个捐献血浆的人，还有一个人为了支付这笔费用打了第二份工。

sentences.en: And many people also charge it on a regular credit card, like a visa, and then pay it off.
sentences.zh: 许多人还用普通的信用卡（比如 Visa）支付，然后再慢慢还清。

sentences.en: But another option that a lot of pet owners end up going for is something called a medical credit card.
sentences.zh: 但许多宠物主人最终选择的另一个方案是所谓的医疗信用卡。

sentences.en: And what exactly is that?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么？

sentences.en: It's a specialty credit card that's offered at a lot of these veterinary clinics.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在许多兽医诊所提供的专业信用卡。

sentences.en: It's right there on the counter often.
sentences.zh: 它通常就放在柜台上。

sentences.en: And the way that these cards generally work is that there's an introductory period, say six months.
sentences.zh: 这些卡通常的运作方式是有一个入门期，比如六个月。

sentences.en: And if you pay that off within that period, you don't have to pay any interest at all.
sentences.zh: 如果你在那段时间内还清了，你根本不需要支付任何利息。

sentences.en: But if you don't pay it off and you still have some debt at the end of that, the interest rate can be pretty serious.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有还清，在期满时仍有欠款，利率可能会非常高。

sentences.en: Like how much?
sentences.zh: 高到什么程度？

sentences.en: Well, I spoke to this one pet owner, her name's Heather Massey, and she shared her bills with me, and she's paying 30%.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我采访了一位宠物主人，她叫 Heather Massey，她和我分享了她的账单，她正在支付 30% 的利息。

sentences.en: Wow, so that's high.
sentences.zh: 哇，那很高了。

sentences.en: Yes, it is high.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实很高。

sentences.en: But you can also see why it's tempting.
sentences.zh: 但你也能看出为什么它很有诱惑力。

sentences.en: You're really struggling to figure out how you can pay off this pretty significant bill.
sentences.zh: 你真的在为如何还清这笔相当大的账单而苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And then, you know, this is an available option to you.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，这是一个摆在你面前的选择。

sentences.en: And, you know, many people think that, hey, I could think I can do that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，很多人会想，嘿，我觉得我可以做到。

sentences.en: I could pay off that during, you know, that six months or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我可以在那六个月左右的时间里还清它。

sentences.en: But Heather is not alone.
sentences.zh: 但 Heather 并不是个例。

sentences.en: I spoke to the company that she got her card through, Care Credit, and they told me that 80% of people who take out the card pay it off in time.
sentences.zh: 我采访了她办卡的这家公司 Care Credit，他们告诉我，80% 的办卡人都能按时还清。

sentences.en: But put another way, that means one in five people who take it out don't pay it off within the introductory period.
sentences.zh: 但换句话说，这意味着五分之一的办卡人没能在入门期内还清。

sentences.en: So a lot of people going into debt for their pets.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人为了宠物背上了债务。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And can I just pause for a moment on that, Katie?
sentences.zh: Katie，我能在这儿暂停一下吗？

sentences.en: I mean, these are dogs and cats, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些是猫和狗，对吧？

sentences.en: These are not our children.
sentences.zh: 它们不是我们的孩子。

sentences.en: And yet we're going into debt like this, trying to prolong their pretty short lives.
sentences.zh: 然而我们却像这样背负债务，试图延长它们短暂的生命。

sentences.en: Like, you know, it does seem kind of nuts in a way.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，这在某种程度上看起来有点疯狂。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, I'm imagining myself in that vet office staring at the bill and staring at a very sick clementine.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你知道，我想象自己在那间兽医诊室里，盯着账单，看着病得很重的 Clementine。

sentences.en: And I think I would have a really hard time not doing that myself, not taking on that debt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果是我，很难不这样做，很难不背上那笔债务。

sentences.en: I can easily imagine myself doing it.
sentences.zh: 我可以很容易地想象自己会这样做。

sentences.en: It's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really hard.
sentences.zh: 是的，真的很难。

sentences.en: And I think we're in a whole new world right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们现在处于一个全新的世界。

sentences.en: You know, the vets that I spoke to used to say that really the only option for a very sick animal was euthanasia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我采访过的兽医过去常说，对于病得很重的动物，唯一的选择就是安乐死。

sentences.en: And now they're going into these exam rooms and offering pet owners so many other options to prolong the life of their dogs and cats.
sentences.zh: 而现在，他们走进检查室，为宠物主人提供了许多其他延长猫狗寿命的选择。

sentences.en: But, you know, regardless of what options these pet owners choose, what's happening is that they're the ones who end up in the driver's seat.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，无论这些宠物主人选择什么方案，事实是他们最终掌握了主动权。

sentences.en: The decision ultimately sits with them and they're now faced with this whole new set of ethical questions and big financial responsibilities that they really never had before.
sentences.zh: 决定权最终掌握在他们手中，他们现在面临着一系列全新的伦理问题和巨大的经济责任，这是他们以前从未遇到过的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like when there's always another treatment to try and there's a credit card to put it on, you know,
sentences.zh: 就像当总有另一种治疗方法可以尝试，而且还有一张信用卡可以支付时，你知道，

sentences.en: it feels to the pet owner like it's their choice about whether their pet lives or dies.
sentences.zh: 对宠物主人来说，这感觉就像是他们在决定宠物的生死。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the question comes up, just because you can, does that mean you should?
sentences.zh: 于是问题就来了，仅仅因为你能做到，就意味着你应该这样做吗？

sentences.en: And is that always in the best interest of the pet?
sentences.zh: 而且这总是符合宠物的最大利益吗？

sentences.en: It's actually the question that I wrestled with my own puppy.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是我在自己的小狗身上纠结过的问题。

sentences.en: He got very sick.
sentences.zh: 它病得很重。

sentences.en: It turned out he had a very serious health problem.
sentences.zh: 结果发现它患有非常严重的健康问题。

sentences.en: And so in our case, we learned that there was a surgery that could fix it.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的案例中，我们得知有一种手术可以治愈它。

sentences.en: Pretty expensive surgery, but we decided to go for it because he was young and had potentially a long dog's life ahead of him.
sentences.zh: 手术费用相当昂贵，但我们决定尝试，因为它还年轻，未来可能还有很长的狗生。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, he experienced complications from the surgery and he didn't actually make it.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，它在手术后出现了并发症，最终没能挺过来。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: But, you know, I don't regret having done it and he got really great care.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我不后悔这样做，它得到了非常好的照顾。

sentences.en: My experience just really echoed what I heard from so many pet owners and veterinarians that there's really no easy answers to these very new questions that we're all facing.
sentences.zh: 我的经历真的呼应了我从许多宠物主人和兽医那里听到的，对于我们所有人现在面临的这些非常新的问题，确实没有简单的答案。

sentences.en: You kind of have to sort out the risks and rewards of pet ownership.
sentences.zh: 你必须权衡养宠物的风险和回报。

sentences.en: And in my case, I decided it was worth it to me.
sentences.zh: 就我而言，我认为这对我来说是值得的。

sentences.en: And I recently got a new dog.
sentences.zh: 而且我最近又养了一只新狗。

sentences.en: So, you know, here we go again.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们又开始了。

sentences.en: Katie, thank you.
sentences.zh: Katie，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday night, amid growing doubts about his age and mental fitness, President Biden wrapped up a summit of NATO leaders in Washington.
sentences.zh: 周四晚上，在对其年龄和精神状态的质疑声中，拜登总统结束了在华盛顿举行的北约领导人峰会。

sentences.en: And now I want to hand it over to the president of Ukraine, who has as much courage as he has determination.
sentences.zh: 现在我想把它交给乌克兰总统，他既有勇气又有决心。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, President Putin.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，普京总统。

sentences.en: By mistakenly introducing the president of Ukraine as the president of Russia.
sentences.zh: 通过错误地将乌克兰总统介绍为俄罗斯总统。

sentences.en: President Putin.
sentences.zh: 普京总统。

sentences.en: You're going to beat President Putin.
sentences.zh: 你会击败普京总统的。

sentences.en: President Zelensky.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基总统。

sentences.en: Later.
sentences.zh: 稍后。

sentences.en: With that, I'll take your questions.
sentences.zh: 就这样，我来回答你们的问题。

sentences.en: I've been given a list of people to call on here.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了一份名单，上面有要点名提问的人。

sentences.en: Biden held a news conference that was widely seen as a crucial test of his stamina and coherence.
sentences.zh: 拜登举行了一场新闻发布会，这被广泛视为对他精力和逻辑连贯性的一次关键考验。

sentences.en: In his first answer, he once again stumbled when referring to his own vice president.
sentences.zh: 在第一个回答中，他在提到自己的副总统时再次口误。

sentences.en: Look, I wouldn't have picked Vice President Trump to be vice president, but I think she was not qualified to be president.
sentences.zh: 听着，我不会选特朗普副总统当副总统，但我认为她没有资格担任总统。

sentences.en: So let's start there.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们从这里开始。

sentences.en: But over the next hour, Biden spoke with fluency and command about the war in Gaza, America's policy toward China, and his relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的一个小时里，拜登就加沙战争、美国的对华政策以及他与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的关系，谈吐流畅且掌控全局。

sentences.en: And when pressed on his age and ability to serve a second term, Biden said he had no reservations.
sentences.zh: 当被追问到他的年龄和是否有能力担任第二个任期时，拜登表示他没有任何顾虑。

sentences.en: And every single day, I'm surrounded by good docs.
sentences.zh: 而且每一天，我都被优秀的医生包围着。

sentences.en: If they think there's a problem, I promise you, or even if they don't think there's a problem, they think I should have a neurological exam again, I'll do it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为有问题，我向你保证，或者即使他们不认为有问题，但他们认为我应该再次进行神经系统检查，我会做的。

sentences.en: No one's suggesting that to me now.
sentences.zh: 现在没有人向我提出这种建议。

sentences.en: Still, when the news conference was over, three more House Democrats called on Biden to step aside as nominee.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在新闻发布会结束后，又有三名民主党众议员呼吁拜登退出竞选。

sentences.en: As of Thursday night, 18 congressional Democrats have asked Biden to end his campaign.
sentences.zh: 截至周四晚上，已有 18 名国会民主党人要求拜登结束他的竞选活动。

sentences.en: A quick reminder to catch a new episode of The Interview right here tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 快速提醒一下，明天在这里收看《The Interview》的新一期节目。

sentences.en: This week, Lulu Garcia Navarro talks with Robert Putnam, the author of Bowling Alone.
sentences.zh: 本周，Lulu Garcia Navarro 将与《独自打保龄球》的作者 Robert Putnam 对话。

sentences.en: For decades, he's been warning about the decline of American community and what that means for our democracy.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他一直在警告美国社区的衰落，以及这对我们的民主意味着什么。

sentences.en: We're not going to fix all these problems in America, polarization, inequality, social isolation, until we start feeling we have an obligation to care for other people.
sentences.zh: 我们无法解决美国所有这些问题，如两极分化、不平等、社会孤立，除非我们开始感到我们有义务去关心他人。

sentences.en: And that's not easy.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Olivia Knatt, Claire Tennisketter, and Ricky Nowetsky, with help from Shannon Lynn.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由 Olivia Knatt、Claire Tennisketter 和 Ricky Nowetsky 制作，Shannon Lynn 提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Diao and Devin Taylor, with research help from Susan Lee.
sentences.zh: 由 Lexi Diao 和 Devin Taylor 编辑，Susan Lee 提供了研究协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell and Rowan Nemesto, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 包含 Dan Powell 和 Rowan Nemesto 的原创音乐，由 Alyssa Moxley 负责工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 的 Jim Brunberg 和 Ben Landsberg 创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Zuzu, Piper, Tiger, Chi-Chi, Zadie, Toby, Gerald, Cosmo, and Clementine.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢 Zuzu、Piper、Tiger、Chi-Chi、Zadie、Toby、Gerald、Cosmo 和 Clementine。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sabrina Tavernisi。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》节目中，我是主持人莎拉·凯尼格，我们将讲述一些人试图维持自身影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
